cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven strip-woven cotton hammock (kpoikpoi) with typical Mende-style supplementary weft patterning in indigo, white and red — a classic Mende textile form used in daily life.

physical.title: hammock; textile
physical.summary: Hammock (kpoikpoi), formed of three wide strips about 23cm wide of hand-spun cotton, which have been hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The ends of the hammock are in white cotton, while the central area on all three strips is completely covered by weft-faced blocks of coloured cotton that form a pattern across the whole in red and two shades of indigo. Within these there are smaller areas with supplementary weft patterns float-woven in indigo and white cotton; some of these are in tapestry-weave. To the sides of the hammock have been sewn six other pieces of woven cloth intended to hang down as flaps (three a side) when the hammock was in use; these are also covered with weft-faced blocks of coloured cotton, and have decorative pompons at the ends. The warp ends of the hammock itself have hand-sewn hems.
